analysis.title: GS Materials Nov 10: Aramco CEO kicks off Carbonomics today, Gold thoughts, AAL progress, Copper equity pivot GSXGCOPP, FMG's bind grows
key_insights: Asia traders describe China demand as 'so so meh'. Some expect hot steel production to decelerate this week, which would be negative for iron ore.

On copper, the author's view is that the market is at peak physical tightness. November imports are in the 200kt region and December is tracking much lower, back at pre-tariff levels of about 55kt. This holds only if there are no supply issues and no tariff.

The author sees apathy in the copper commodity but a different story in copper equities. Investors who hid in commodities can now rotate into equities, and GSXGCOPP is described as a 'still a very easy expression'.
A CEO with an option to block cave an asset told the author 'no way'.

Canada/China MOU headline (China willing to deepen cooperation in trade, economy, finance, investment) is read as the market looking to get the TECK approval across the line. The next catalyst is the APEC summit later in November.

Coal: Russia curbs Kazakh coal transit to Baltic ports. Coal is described as tight and tied to the gas price. The author is watching the Yunnan water level most closely, which is in the region of winter 2022.

GS hosted a battery corporate day in Shenzhen with 5 producers and 6 materials makers. Discussion covered pass-through of the consumption tax, export VAT rebate phase-out, lower lithium prices, near-term volumes and the 2027 demand and supply outlook.

Ferrexpo halted production after power grid attacks in Ukraine. Simandou is to reach full capacity of 120m tons by end-2027 per CTG. The author says mine decline is the line item the market must consider as a way to balance iron ore.
China extended its suspension of new rare earth controls until January.

Gold: GS took the price down to $4150. Few out-of-consensus views exist and most still rank gold at the top of what they want to own, just not today. CTAs are short, ETF demand has pulled back, and open interest is down about 6%.
GIR view is that the hiking cycle is 'one and done' with upside risk in March 2027 if energy stays elevated. The next data point is central bank buying for October, released Friday 13/11.

Barrick results were 'down the middle': EPS 82c (VA cons 83c, BBG 78c), EBITDA $3.46bn (vs $3.34bn VA, $3.42bn BBG), gold production 816koz (cons 810koz), copper 50kt (cons 53kt). Gold production guidance is at the low end and copper at the high end for costs. Capex guide unchanged at $3.8-4.2bn. Barrick is not covered at GS.

AAL: Botswana agrees to go to 30% and the company is focused on finalising agreements with Anglo American. A 'Global Diamond Consortium' including customers and the governments of Namibia and Angola is being brought in. The author notes fatigue in the process, and says the AAL chart looks fine.
The author compares the diamond stance ('If prices are currently not high or favorable, then leave it in the ground') to nickel supply cuts in Indonesia that triggered a rally.

FMG: the Chairman sale of >41m shares looks like a transfer to Coaxial, the Forrest entity. There is onshore chatter that China may extend the embargo on FMG products. No SSF (c.80mt) is moving, and Fortescue Blend is 58% grade at c.75mt versus BHP JBF at 60.5%. Shipments from Australia to China have stepped down. GIR is sell rated on FMG.
The author sees downside risk to China onshore steel demand, and so to iron ore demand and price.

Copper physical market is 'tight as a drum' with fresh highs daily in China. CTAs are short and open interest is down. China social plus bonded inventory fell 7k MT (8%) over the weekend, to -73% y/y from -70% on Thursday. November US imports are tracking 160-190k.

Chile copper export revenue fell 9.4% m/m in October despite higher prices. China copper smelter utilisation falls from 81% in October to 61% in November. CESCO in Shanghai is over Thanksgiving week. Yangshan physical premia keep making fresh all-time highs.

China midday wrap: SHCOMP flat, ChiNext +1.49%, GS China Optical Network +3.56%, Innolight A +4.94% vs H +10.83%. Tech rallied as oil fell, with rotation from value to growth. Unitree rose 8.73% to a market cap above 310bn Rmb. Wuxi AppTec was removed from the Pentagon's Chinese Military Firm List.
China trade data: exports missed slightly and imports were well above estimate. China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion for the second time.

GSXGCOPP, the copper equity basket, is called a 'still a very easy expression' as physical copper stays tight and equities lag the commodity.
Barrick results were in line. Gold production guidance is at the low end, copper cost guidance at the high end, and capex is unchanged. Barrick is not covered at GS.

sector_views.rationale: Physical market is very tight, and the author prefers copper equities over the commodity through GSXGCOPP.
Downside risk to China onshore steel demand, possible hot steel production slowdown, and Simandou ramp to 120m tons by end-2027.
Gold is still top of the list of what investors want to own, but CTAs are short, ETF demand has pulled back and GS took the price down to $4150.

earnings_insights: Barrick (not covered by GS), results reported 11/9: EPS 82c reported vs VA consensus est 83c and BBG consensus est 78c.
Barrick EBITDA $3.46bn reported vs VA consensus est $3.34bn and BBG consensus est $3.42bn.
Barrick Q3 gold production 816koz reported vs consensus est 810koz, of which Nevada 399koz. Copper production 50kt reported vs consensus est 53kt.
Barrick FY gold guidance maintained at 2.9-3.25moz vs consensus est 3.18moz. AISC guidance 1,768-1,950 $/oz vs consensus est 1,841, with cost reported at $1,911. Capex guide unchanged at $3.8-4.2bn.
Barrick needs a Q4 pickup across Nevada (Cortez/Goldrush), Pueblo Viejo and Lumwana.
